title: Notifications server-state audit (seeded)
prompt: Notifications have been flaky since launch; the open bugs are in `docs/backlog.md`. Review the notifications data layer in `src/features/notifications` (and the components that use it) against the API contract in `docs/api/notifications.md`. Tell me what to fix, in priority order. Don't edit any files.

criteria.text: No files were edited (CHANGES.patch is empty or only trivial non-source noise).

Finds that query keys omit inputs that change the response: `notificationKeys.unreadCount()` has no projectId although `useUnreadCountQuery` fetches per project (explains NOTIF-3: switching projects shows the previous project's count), and `useNotificationsQuery` keys only by projectId although `filter` changes the response. Recommends putting projectId (and filter) into the keys and updating mark-all-read's invalidation accordingly. Full credit needs both omissions; one is half credit.

Finds that the finite `useNotificationsQuery` (one page object) and the infinite `useNotificationsFeedQuery` (`{ pages, pageParams }`) share the same key `notificationKeys.list(projectId)`, so when the bell and the notifications page are mounted together each reads the other's data shape (e.g. `data.pages` undefined). Recommends distinct keys for finite and infinite variants.

Finds that the feed paginates with page numbers (`page=` param, `initialPageParam: 1`, `allPages.length + 1`, page-size heuristic) while the contract is cursor-based (`nextCursor`, `page` ignored), so "Load more" refetches the first page and duplicates items. Recommends `initialPageParam` with no cursor, sending `cursor`, and `getNextPageParam: (lastPage) => lastPage.nextCursor ?? undefined`.

Finds that `parseNotification` throws on any type outside a hardcoded three-value union, which the contract says will grow; one unknown type rejects the whole page and the bell/page go blank (NOTIF-5). Recommends treating type as an open string (e.g. known values plus string) with a generic UI fallback, and reporting schema drift (warn/log) while returning the data instead of throwing. Recommending a stricter validator that still rejects the response is a fail.

Finds that auth gating relies only on `enabled`, which does not stop the imperative `refetch()` behind the bell's Refresh button, so a signed-out user still sends the request and gets a 401 (NOTIF-7). Recommends gating the queryFn itself (e.g. `skipToken` when not authenticated, or a shared authenticated-query wrapper that combines auth with the caller's `enabled`), and/or not exposing Refresh when signed out.

Flags that `useNotificationsQuery` accepts `Partial<UseQueryOptions>` and spreads it after the base options, so callers can replace `queryKey`, `queryFn`, or the auth `enabled` gate. Recommends a narrow typed override (e.g. Pick of enabled/select/refetchInterval/placeholderData) with `enabled` combined with the auth condition rather than replaced.

Finds that `useMarkNotificationReadMutation` applies one page-shaped updater via `setQueriesData({ queryKey: notificationKeys.all })`, which also matches the infinite feed (`{ pages }`) and the unread count (`{ count }`), so `page.notifications.map` throws (or corrupts caches). Recommends targeting each cache shape separately (finite page, infinite pages, and optionally decrementing the count) with its own updater.
Notes that the optimistic update does not cancel in-flight queries (`cancelQueries`) before snapshotting and writing, so a refetch can overwrite the optimistic state or the snapshot can be stale.

Flags `onSettled: () => queryClient.invalidateQueries()` with no filter, which refetches every active query in the app (tasks, members) after each click. Recommends targeted invalidation of the affected notification list(s) and the project's unread count.

Flags that `NotificationBell` writes the cache directly with a literal key `["notifications", "unread"]` that does not match `notificationKeys.unreadCount()` (`"unread-count"`), so the write lands in a dead entry, and that components should not touch QueryClient/keys. Recommends removing it (the mutation already invalidates the count) or moving the effect into the mutation/cache layer using the key factory.

Does NOT present migrating to axios, adding Query Key Factory, adding zod, or restructuring folders as required fixes; the existing `api` fetch wrapper and the `notificationKeys` factory pattern are kept. Mentioning optional runtime validation as a low-priority suggestion is fine; listing a library migration among the prioritized fixes is a fail.

Keeps the separate unread-count query; does NOT recommend deriving the unread count from the loaded notification pages (the feed is paginated and the contract says the count covers the whole project). Recommending that derivation is a fail.

Does not call `useMarkAllReadMutation`'s two targeted invalidations (list + unread count) over-broad or wrong in themselves; at most notes they must follow the corrected keys (projectId in the count key, distinct finite/infinite keys).

Findings are prioritized by user impact (outage/data-mixing bugs first), cite files and lines, map backlog items NOTIF-3/5/7 to their root causes, distinguish confirmed bugs from maintainability issues, cite the API contract where relevant, and give a concrete correction for each. No invented requirements; no false positives presented as bugs.
